drug_class: Nrf2 activator (nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 activator)
purpose: Omaveloxolone is used to treat Friedreich's ataxia, a rare genetic disease that affects movement and coordination, in adults and teenagers aged 16 and older. It helps slow down the worsening of symptoms related to balance and walking. This is currently the first FDA-approved medicine specifically for this condition.
how_it_works: Your body has a natural protection system that fights inflammation and oxidative stress, which is damage caused by harmful molecules called free radicals. In Friedreich's ataxia, this protective system does not work well because a protein called frataxin is missing. Omaveloxolone activates a key switch in your cells called Nrf2, which helps turn on your body's natural defenses to reduce damage to nerve and heart cells.
common_side_effects: The most common side effects include nausea, stomach pain, fatigue or tiredness, diarrhea, constipation, headache, and urinary tract infections. Some patients also experience increased liver enzyme levels, so your doctor will monitor your liver with blood tests. You may also notice muscle pain or weakness.
warnings: This medicine can raise liver enzyme levels, which may be a sign of liver stress, so regular blood tests are very important. It may also increase cholesterol and triglyceride levels in your blood. Women who are pregnant or planning to become pregnant should talk to their doctor, as this medicine may harm an unborn baby. It can also interact with certain other medications, so always tell your doctor and pharmacist everything you are taking.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is 150 mg taken by mouth once daily with food. Taking it with food helps reduce stomach-related side effects. Try to take it at the same time each day, and if you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember unless it is almost time for your next dose — in that case, just skip the missed dose and continue your regular schedule.
